source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m near-real-time, NOAA-20 + NOAA-21, 7-day global files
limitations: Not every detection is a wildfire: agricultural burns, gas flares and industrial heat are also detected. Nothing here states a cause.
Satellite limits: a place is seen only a few times per day, cloud and thick smoke hide fires, and each pixel is about 375 m wide.
NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 fly about 50 minutes apart, so one fire can appear twice. Counts are detections, not unique fires.
This is near-real-time (NRT) data, not science-quality data.
The window is only about 7 days. The trend flag is a short-term signal, not a trend.
Priority score weights (0.5 FRP, 0.2 count, 0.3 trend) are a starting choice, not validated. The score ranks regions against each other; it is not a risk measure.
Total FRP is approximate: neighbouring pixels often share identical FRP values (cause unconfirmed).
Days are UTC. Late-evening detections in India fall on the next UTC day.
Regions come from Natural Earth 10 m boundaries. Fires on the coast, offshore or on a border can be left Unassigned.
Suggested checks are prompts for a human to look at, not official protocols.
